summary.short: New York S3008C adds consumer rules for personalized algorithmic pricing (disclosure of algorithm use, personal data and prices) and AI companion models (suicide-detection protocols and not-human notices), enforced by the attorney general with civil penalties. Part X takes effect on the sixtieth day after enactment.
summary.long: Part X adds General Business Law § 349-a on personalized algorithmic pricing, defining algorithm, personal data, dynamic pricing and personalized algorithmic pricing. Providers must disclose that they use such pricing, disclose the personal data used to set it, and give a clear and conspicuous disclosure of the price. After a consumer report, the attorney general may send a cease and desist letter and then seek an injunction; courts may impose civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Part U adds General Business Law Article 47 on AI companion models, defining AI companions as systems that retain personal information, ask unprompted emotion-based questions and sustain ongoing personal dialogue, and excluding customer-service, efficiency or research tools and internal business systems. Operators must maintain a protocol to detect suicidal ideation or self-harm and refer users to crisis services, and must tell users at the start of an interaction that they are not communicating with a human; such notices need not exceed once per day and must recur at least every three hours in continuing interactions. The attorney general may seek injunctions and civil penalties of up to $15,000 per day; fines are deposited in a suicide prevention fund created by State Finance Law § 99-ss. The excerpt gives no effective date for Part U.

relations.note: Part X renumbers GBL § 349-a as § 349-h and adds a new § 349-a on personalized algorithmic pricing; Part U adds a new article 47 (§§ 1700-1704) on AI companion models.

notes: Document combines two Parts of S3008C: Part X (GBL § 349-a, personalized algorithmic pricing) and Part U (GBL article 47, AI companion models, plus State Finance Law § 99-ss). Part X takes effect on the sixtieth day after becoming law; no effective date for Part U appears in the provided text. Penalties differ between Parts: Part X civil penalty up to one thousand dollars per violation; Part U up to fifteen thousand dollars per day for violations of §§ 1701 or 1702. The text ends during § 99-ss(1); later subsections were not reviewed. Operators are a defined class, not named entities. evidence.quote: Any personalized algorithmic pricing provider shall:
(a) "Algorithm" means a computational automated process that uses a set of rules to define a sequence of operations.
"Clear and conspicuous disclosure" means disclosure in the same medium as, and provided on, at, or near and contemporaneous with every advertisement
"Consumer" means a natural person who is seeking or solicited to purchase, lease or receive a good or service for personal, family or household use.
"Personal data" means any data that identifies or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a specific consumer or device.
"Dynamic pricing" means pricing that fluctuates dependent on current market conditions.
"Personalized algorithmic pricing" means dynamic pricing set by an algorithm that uses personal data as defined in this section.
"Personalized algorithmic pricing provider" means any person, partnership, corporation, association or other entity that uses personalized algorithmic pricing.

"Artificial intelligence", "artificial intelligence technology", or "AI" means a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions
"Generative artificial intelligence" means a class of AI models that emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content

"AI model" means a component of an information system that implements artificial intelligence technology and uses computational, statistical, or machine-learning techniques to produce outputs from a given set of inputs.

"AI companion" means a system using artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, and/or emotional recognition algorithms designed to simulate a sustained human or human-like relationship with a user by:
"Operator" means any person, partnership, association, firm, or business entity, or any member, affiliate, subsidiary or beneficial owner
"Person" means any natural person.
"Emotional recognition algorithms" means artificial intelligence that detects and interprets human emotional signals in text
"User" means any person who uses an AI companion for personal use within the state and who is not an operator or agent or affiliate of the operator of the AI companion.
"Self-harm" means intentional self-injury with or without the intent to cause death.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier or prohibition was found. The civil penalty amounts (not more than $1,000 per violation under § 349-a; up to $15,000 per day under § 1703) are enforcement. The five-day notice, the designated cease-and-desist timeline and the notification timing in § 1702 (at least every three hours, need not exceed once per day) are procedural or obligation parameters.
